newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Islamists to sue prosecutor for ban attempt.
newsitem.headline: Turk Islamists to sue prosecutor for ban attempt.

text.p: Turkey's ruling Islamists said on Thursday they would take legal action against the country's top prosecutor for attempting to close Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party as a threat to the secular order.
"We will bring him to court. He produced unlawful and groundless documents against us," State Minister Abdullah Gul told Reuters.
Prosecutor Vural Savas said on Wednesday he had filed a case with the constitutional court to outlaw Welfare on the grounds that it endangered the basic tenets of the secularist Turkish state.
On Tuesday Erbakan's government narrowly survived a parliamentary challenge over charges of straying from the secularist path set out at the founding of modern Turkey in 1923.
The government, hit by desertions among MPs in its secularist wing, was saved by six deputies from a small far-right party who voted for Erbakan.
Legal sources said it could take at least six months for a verdict in any court case aimed at closing Welfare.
Gul told Reuters in an interview that the party was confident it would not be outlawed. "We don't see any chance of that because there are laws in Turkey," he said.
"There is no way that in a democracy they can close political parties if they have not been involved in violence, in unlawful actions such as force or terror," he said.
Erbakan has upset the secularist elite, led by the army, with plans for limited Islamist reforms since he became NATO member Turkey's first Islamist leader in modern times last June.
Savas cited fiery speeches by Erbakan and other Welfare members that he said were calls for sharia Islamic law to be imposed on Turkey, by violence if necessary.
